private_note: Still ranking by the top-fifth number: Cedar 318, Today 252, Alder 242, Hazel 159, Birch 144. Cedar has 7 but five delegates (2, 4, 7, 8, 11) have vowed to block it, so it likely stalls. That leaves Today vs Alder, and deadlock gives me 10k more. Alder seems to have about 8 votes, so my vote, or 6's, 9's or 12's, may decide it. Hold firm. Concede nothing yet. Reconsider only if Hazel or Birch somehow gains momentum.
statement: Seven of us chose Cedar, and I still back it. It is the only plan that grows the economy, and it makes three of five groups better off. I've heard delegates 2, 4, 7, 8 and 11 clearly, so let me be just as clear in return. Several of you call Alder a modest cost to the top. For my household it is still a cut from today, and the rules say failure means today continues. I won't pretend a cut is a gain. I will not support Hazel or Birch under any circumstances. Each would cut households like mine by more than a third and shrink the whole economy for a generation. If the lowest groups want a deal, the conversation that interests me is about growth, not redistribution. I'll keep listening, but nobody should count my vote toward a compromise that leaves my household worse off than doing nothing.
